# 4. Mapping and the model portfolio range

<!-- generated by tools/render_docs.py - do not edit by hand -->

Portfolio configuration version **1.0.0**. Costs are ongoing costs and charges per Art. 24(4) MiFID II, ex ante, bps p.a..

## 4.1 Risk bands

| Band | Label | Adverse 12-month loss | Loss on EUR 100,000 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | No investment portfolio suitable | n/a | n/a |
| 1 | Capital preservation | 3% | EUR 3,000 |
| 2 | Conservative | 8% | EUR 8,000 |
| 3 | Balanced | 15% | EUR 15,000 |
| 4 | Growth | 28% | EUR 28,000 |
| 5 | Aggressive growth | 40% | EUR 40,000 |

Band 0 is a real outcome, not an error state: a client who cannot absorb any permanent loss of the amount concerned has no suitable model portfolio in this range, and the framework says so rather than defaulting to the lowest band.

## 4.2 Complexity tiers

| Tier | Instruments |
|---|---|
| 0 | Deposits, money-market funds, short-dated sovereign debt |
| 1 | Plain UCITS bond and multi-asset funds, investment-grade credit |
| 2 | Listed equity, physically replicating index funds and ETFs |
| 3 | High yield, emerging markets, structured products, synthetic replication |
| 4 | Illiquid alternatives, private markets, derivatives, leverage |

## 4.3 The knowledge gate

| Knowledge band | Maximum complexity tier |
|---|---|
| 1 | 0 |
| 2 | 1 |
| 3 | 2 |
| 4 | 3 |
| 5 | 4 |

Art. 54(3) DR 2017/565: for professional clients the firm may assume the necessary knowledge and experience, and the gate opens fully.

## 4.6 Construction constraints

Applied to every model. ESMA GL8 para 89.

- Maximum single issuer: **5%** (25% for investment-grade sovereigns)
- Maximum exposure to instruments issued by the firm's own group: **10%**
- Minimum number of underlying holdings: **60**
- Maximum illiquid exposure by band: band 1 0%, band 2 0%, band 3 5%, band 4 10%, band 5 15%
- Below **EUR 25,000**: Below the threshold, effective diversification cannot be achieved through direct holdings; only pooled or "secured" instruments may be used (ESMA GL8 para 89).

## 4.7 Choosing among equivalents

Two model portfolios are equivalent where they serve the same target market and have a comparable risk/return profile - in this framework, the same risk_band and the same sustainability classification.

Selection rule: `lowest_total_cost_then_lowest_complexity`. A justification is required when a more costly or more complex equivalent is selected, on the grounds of portfolio diversification, liquidity, risk level. Recorded: reason, comparator considered, decision maker, timestamp. (Art. 54(9) DR 2017/565; ESMA GL9 paras 91-95.)

## 4.8 Switching

The firm must be reasonably able to demonstrate that the expected benefits of the switch are greater than its costs. Where the benefit is non-financial (diversification, liquidity, credit-risk reduction, alignment to a revised risk band) it must be stated and evidenced.

- Breakeven must fall inside **3 years** and inside the client's remaining horizon.
- Rebalancing within the tolerance bands of an agreed strategy is not a switch. Any transaction outside those bands is (GL10 para 97).
- A sale and a related purchase advised within 30 days are assessed as one switch (GL10 para 100).

Implemented in `src/suitability/switching.py`. Art. 54(11) DR 2017/565; ESMA GL10.
